items.skill: Climbs on a chair or other elevated piece of furniture (e.g. a bed) without help
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Walks backwards
items.proc:
MATERIALS: toy
PROCEDURE: Ask the student to walk backwards by demonstrating this. Credit if the student walks backwards without falling or holding on to anything.
Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Runs without tripping or falling
items.proc:
MATERIALS: ball
PROCEDURE: Encourage the student to run by rolling a ball across the floor. Credit if the student can run fast and smoothly without tripping or falling.

items.skill: Walks down stairs, 2 feet on each step, with one hand held
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Walks up stairs holding the handrail, 2 feet on each step
items.proc:
MATERIALS: toy
PROCEDURE: Place a toy in the middle of the steps and ask the student to walk up the stairs to get it. Credit if the student walks up using the handrail or wall for support and places both feet on each step before stepping on the next one.
Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Walks upstairs with alternate feet without holding the handrail
items.proc:
MATERIALS: toy
PROCEDURE: Place a toy in the middle of the steps and ask the student to walk upstairs to get it. Credit if the student walks upstairs alternating feet on each successive step without holding the handrail or wall for support.
Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Walks downstairs with alternate feet without holding the handrail
items.proc:
MATERIALS: toy
PROCEDURE: Place a toy in the middle of the steps and ask the student to walk downstairs to get it. Credit if the student walks downstairs alternating feet on each successive step without holding the handrail or wall. Do not credit if the student places both feet on a step or uses the handrail or wall for support.
Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Moves body part as directed
items.proc: PROCEDURE: Ask the student to raise both arms.

items.skill: Jumps up
items.proc: This must be elicited by the examiner.

items.skill: Throws a ball overhead with direction
items.proc:
MATERIALS: ball
PROCEDURE: Give the student the ball and stand at least 3 feet (1 metre) away. Ask the student to throw the ball to you using an overhead throw. You may show the student how to do it. Credit if the student throws the ball within your arm's reach, between your knees and head, using an overhand throw and not sideways or underhand.

items.skill: Hops 1 to 3 steps on preferred foot
items.proc: PROCEDURE: Ask the student to lift one foot and hop at least three times on the preferred foot. Credit if the student hops at least three times on the preferred foot without holding on to anything.

items.skill: Jumps and turns
items.proc: PROCEDURE: Ask the student to jump while making a half-turn. Credit if the student can do this without tripping or falling.

items.skill: Dances patterns / joins group movement activities
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Uses all 5 fingers to get food/toys placed on a flat surface
items.proc:
MATERIALS: small toy/object
PROCEDURE: Seat the student on the parent's lap with elbows level with the table top and hands on the table or flat surface. Drop a small toy in front of the student and attract attention by pointing to the toy or tapping the surface. Credit if the student picks up the toy using all 5 fingers as if raking.

items.skill: Picks up objects with thumb and index finger
items.proc:
MATERIALS: any small toy or food
PROCEDURE: Place a toy/food in front of the student and within reach. Attract attention by tapping near the toy/food. Credit if the student uses the tips of the thumb and index or forefinger to pick up the toy/food.

items.skill: Displays a definite hand preference
items.proc:
MATERIALS: toy
PROCEDURE: Place the toy directly in front of the student at midline (not to the left or right) and ask the student to reach for it. Credit if the student uses the same hand 2 out of 3 times.
Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Puts small objects in/out of containers
items.proc:
MATERIALS: small objects, container
This must be elicited by the examiner.

items.skill: Holds a crayon with all the fingers of the hand making a fist (palmar grasp)
items.proc:
MATERIALS: crayon
PROCEDURE: Present the student with a crayon and have them take it. Credit if the student holds it by wrapping all 5 fingers around it as if making a fist. Automatically credit this item if the student uses the tips of all 5 fingers or the thumb, index and middle fingers.
This must be elicited by the examiner.

items.skill: Unscrews the lid of a container or unwraps food
items.proc:
MATERIALS: container with screw-on top or wrapped sweet
This must be elicited by the examiner.

items.skill: Scribbles spontaneously
items.proc:
MATERIALS: paper, pencil/crayon
PROCEDURE: Place paper and a pencil/crayon on the table or flat surface and ask the student to draw anything they want without showing them what to do. Credit if the student uses the tips of the thumb and any other fingertips to grasp the pencil/crayon and makes purposeful marks on the paper (not accidental marks).

items.skill: Scribbles vertical and horizontal lines
items.proc:
MATERIALS: paper, pencil/crayon
PROCEDURE: Place paper and a pencil/crayon on the table and ask the student to draw vertical and horizontal lines after you have demonstrated these. Credit if the student produces a vertical or horizontal line at least 2 inches (5 cm) long that does not vary from your line by more than 30 degrees. The lines may be wavy but not broken.

items.skill: Draws a circle purposely
items.proc:
MATERIALS: paper, pencil/crayon
PROCEDURE: Place paper and a pencil/crayon on the table and ask the student to draw a circle or a ball after you have demonstrated it. Credit if the student produces any curve that is closed or nearly closed. Continuous spiral motions are not credited.

items.skill: Draws a human figure (head, eyes, trunk, arms, hands/fingers)
items.proc:
MATERIALS: paper, pencil
PROCEDURE: Give the student a pencil and paper and ask them to draw a picture of a person. Credit if the student draws 3 or more body parts. A pair is considered one part (eyes, ears, arms, hands, legs and feet).

items.skill: Draws a house using geometric forms
items.proc:
MATERIALS: paper, pencil
PROCEDURE: Give the student a pencil and paper and ask them to draw a picture of a house. Credit if the student has drawn at least the roof, main frame, and a door or window.

items.skill: Feeds self with finger food (e.g. biscuits, bread) using fingers
items.proc:
MATERIALS: bread, biscuits
This must be elicited by the examiner.

items.skill: Feeds self using fingers with spillage
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Feeds self using a spoon with spillage
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Feeds self using fingers without spillage
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Feeds self using a spoon without spillage
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Eats without needing to be spoon-fed during any meal
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Helps hold a cup for drinking
items.proc: Note: The cup should not have a lid or spout.

items.skill: Drinks from a cup with spillage
items.proc: Ask the parent/caregiver if the student can drink from a cup/glass with some spillage. The cup should not have a lid or spout.

items.skill: Drinks from a cup unassisted
items.proc:
MATERIALS: drinking cup, water
This must be elicited by the examiner.

items.skill: Gets a drink for self unassisted
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Pours from a jug without spillage
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Prepares own food/snack
items.proc: Ask the parent/caregiver if the student can prepare their own snack without help, except for getting items that are hard to reach (e.g. bowl, spoon).

items.skill: Prepares food for younger siblings/family members when no adult is around
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Participates when being dressed (e.g. raises arms or lifts leg)
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Pulls down elastic-waist shorts
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Removes a vest or T-shirt
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Dresses without assistance except for buttons and tying
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Dresses without assistance, including buttons and tying
items.proc:
MATERIALS: small shirt with buttons and a shoelace
PROCEDURE: Have the student demonstrate how to button in order to credit this item.

items.skill: Informs the adult only after having already urinated or moved bowels in their underwear
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Informs an adult of the need to urinate or move bowels so they can be taken to the toilet
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Goes to the toilet to urinate or move bowels, but sometimes still does this in their underwear
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Goes to the toilet to urinate or move bowels and never does this in their underwear anymore
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Wipes/cleans self after a bowel movement
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Participates when bathing (e.g. rubbing arms with soap)
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Washes and dries hands without any help
items.proc: Ask the parent/caregiver if the student can wash and dry their hands without any help or supervision, except to turn on/off taps that are out of reach.

items.skill: Washes face without any help
items.proc: Ask the parent/caregiver if the student can wash and dry their face without any help or supervision, except to turn on/off taps that are out of reach.

items.skill: Bathes without any help
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Points to a family member when asked to do so
items.proc: PROCEDURE: Ask the student to point to their mother/caregiver. Credit if they do so.

items.skill: Points to 5 body parts on self when asked to do so
items.proc: PROCEDURE: Have the student point to their eyes, nose, mouth, hands and feet. Credit if they can point to all of these.

items.skill: Points to 5 named pictured objects when asked to do so
items.proc:
MATERIALS: picture book
PROCEDURE: Show the student a picture book (one picture per page) and ask them to point to the picture by saying "Where's the ____?" ("____ iko wapi?"). Credit if the student can use a finger to point to at least 5 pictures.

items.skill: Follows one-step instructions that include simple prepositions (e.g. in, on, under)
items.proc:
MATERIALS: block/toy
PROCEDURE: Ask the student to put a block/toy under the table; on the table; in the bag. Do not point or use gestures when giving the instructions. Credit if the student is able to follow at least one of the instructions.

items.skill: Follows 2-step instructions that include simple prepositions
items.proc:
MATERIALS: block/toy
PROCEDURE: Ask the student to get a block/toy from under the table and then place it on the table. Do not point or use gestures when giving the instruction. Credit if the student is able to follow.

items.skill: Uses 5-20 recognisable words
items.proc: PROCEDURE: Ask the parent/caregiver if the student can clearly say 5-6 words aside from "mama" and "baba". This is the minimum number.

items.skill: Uses pronouns (e.g. I, me, mine / mimi, yangu)
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Uses 2-3 word verb-noun combinations (e.g. "want milk" / "nataka maziwa")
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Names objects in pictures
items.proc:
MATERIALS: picture book
PROCEDURE: Show the student a picture book, point to an object in the book, then ask them to name it (e.g. "What is this?" / "Hii ni nini?"). Credit if the student can say the correct name of at least 4 objects.

items.skill: Speaks in grammatically correct 2-3 word sentences
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Asks "what" questions
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Asks "who" and "why" questions
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Gives an account of recent experiences (with prompting) in order of occurrence using the past tense
items.proc:
PROCEDURE: Ask the parent/caregiver if the student can recount recent experiences in the correct sequence and using the past tense correctly. The caregiver can prompt so the student can complete what they are talking about (e.g. "then what happened?" / "halafu nini kilitokea?").
Parent report will suffice.

domains.name: Cognitive
domains.title: Cognitive Domain
domains.note: Item 2 is not present in the source Form 2; the original numbering has been kept so raw scores match the conversion tables.

items.skill: Looks in the direction of a fallen object
items.proc:
MATERIALS: spoon/ball
PROCEDURE: With the student seated, get their attention and drop a spoon/ball in front of them. Observe if their eyes look down as it falls. Credit if the student brings their eyes and head down as the object falls.

items.skill: Imitates behaviour just seen a few minutes earlier
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Offers an object but will not release it
Looks for a completely hidden object
items.proc:
MATERIALS: ball, small towel/cloth
PROCEDURE: With the student facing you, hide a ball completely under a small towel and observe if they will look under the towel. Credit if the student looks under the towel and gets the hidden ball.

items.skill: Exhibits simple pretend play (e.g. feeds a doll, puts a doll to sleep)
items.proc:
MATERIALS: doll or toy car/block
PROCEDURE: Carry the doll and try to rock it to sleep, or move the toy car/block back and forth. Credit if the student can imitate this.

items.skill: Matches objects
items.proc:
MATERIALS: pairs of spoons, balls, blocks
PROCEDURE: Place one spoon, one ball and one block on the table. Give the student the other set of objects arranged in random order. Demonstrate a matching response (e.g. spoon to spoon) then return the objects to the student. Say, "Put each object on the one that is just like it." Credit if the student can match the objects correctly.

items.skill: Matches 2-3 colours
items.proc:
MATERIALS: 3 pairs of crayons (blue, red, yellow)
PROCEDURE: Place one crayon of each colour on the table. Give the student the other crayons arranged in random order. Demonstrate a matching response (e.g. red crayon with another red crayon) then return the crayons to the student. Say, "Put each crayon on the one that is just like it." Credit if the student can match.

items.skill: Matches pictures
items.proc:
MATERIALS: 3 pairs of picture cards (e.g. pictures of an apple, orange, banana)
PROCEDURE: Place one copy of each picture on the table. Give the student the other pictures arranged in random order. Demonstrate a matching response (e.g. apple with another apple) then return the pictures to the student. Say, "Put each picture on the one that is just like it." Credit if the student can match all the pictures correctly.

items.skill: Sorts based on shapes
items.proc:
MATERIALS: 4 pairs of different shapes that are of the same size and colour
PROCEDURE: Show the student the shapes. Tell the student, "Put together the ones that are the same." After the student sorts and groups the shapes, point to the ones with the same shape and ask, "Why did you put these together?" Credit if the student can group the same shapes and say why they are the same (e.g. "they are the same", "same shape", "all circles").

items.skill: Sorts objects based on 2 attributes (e.g. size and colour)
items.proc:
MATERIALS: 4 pairs of the same shape that differ in size and colour
PROCEDURE: Show the student the shapes. Tell the student, "Put together the ones that are the same." Credit if the student can sort all the shapes according to size and colour.

items.skill: Arranges objects according to size from smallest to biggest
items.proc:
MATERIALS: 4 pieces of graduated-size squares and 4 pieces of graduated-size circles
PROCEDURE: Show the student the first set of squares spread out at random on the table. Say, "Here are 4 squares. Look, I can begin with the smallest, then the next big one, until the biggest one." Demonstrate how to arrange the squares. Then disarrange these and tell the student, "Now you start with the smallest, put the next one and the next big one until the last one." Repeat this procedure using the circles without demonstrating. Credit if the student arranges at least one set of shapes in correct order from smallest to biggest. Allow one trial for each set of shapes.

items.skill: Names 4-6 colours
items.proc:
MATERIALS: 6 papers of different colours
PROCEDURE: Ask the student, "What colour is this?" Credit if the student can name 4-6 colours correctly.

items.skill: Copies shapes
items.proc:
MATERIALS: paper and pen/crayon
PROCEDURE: Let the student copy a circle, triangle and square after demonstrating how each of these is done.

items.skill: Names 3 animals or vegetables when asked
States what common household items are used for
items.proc: Credit if the student can state the use or function of at least 2 household items, e.g. a bed and a drinking glass.

items.skill: Can assemble simple puzzles
items.proc: MATERIALS: simple 4-6 piece puzzles

items.skill: Demonstrates an understanding of opposites by completing a statement (e.g. "The elephant is big, the mouse is ____" / "Tembo ni mkubwa, panya ni ____")
Points to left and right sides of the body
items.proc: PROCEDURE: Sit across from the student and ask, "Show me your left hand." Do the same for the following: right hand, left foot, right knee, left shoulder, right eye, right knee, left leg. Credit if the student can correctly point out the left and right side on at least 5 body parts as requested.

items.skill: Can state what is silly or wrong with pictures (e.g. "What is wrong with this picture?" / "Kuna nini kibaya kwenye picha hii?")
items.proc:
MATERIALS: a picture
PROCEDURE: Show the pictured scenes to the student one at a time and ask, "What is wrong with this picture?" Credit if the student correctly identifies what made the picture incorrect.

items.skill: Matches upper and lower case letters
items.proc: MATERIALS: alphabet cards with upper and lower case letters

items.skill: Enjoys watching activities of nearby people or animals
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Friendly with strangers but initially may show slight anxiety or shyness
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Plays alone but likes to be near familiar adults or brothers and sisters
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Laughs or squeals aloud in play
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Plays peek-a-boo
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Rolls a ball interactively with caregiver/examiner
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Hugs or cuddles toys
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Demonstrates respect for elders (e.g. greets with "Shikamoo" and responds politely)
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Shares toys with others
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Imitates adult activities (e.g. cooking, washing)
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Identifies feelings in others
items.proc:
Credit if the student can tell when the caregiver is feeling happy, sad, worried, etc.
Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Appropriately uses cultural gestures of greeting without much prompting (e.g. handshake, "Shikamoo" with a bow, hug)
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Comforts playmates/siblings in distress
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Persists when faced with a problem or obstacle to their wants
items.proc: Credit if the student tries to solve the problem instead of crying when something stands in the way of what they want (e.g. fastening a box of their treasures with a string if the lid no longer closes).

items.skill: Helps with family chores (e.g. wiping tables, watering plants)
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Curious about the environment but knows when to stop asking questions of adults
items.proc: Credit if the student asks questions about things around them but knows when they are pestering an adult about the topic.

items.skill: Waits for their turn
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Asks permission to play with a toy being used by another
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Defends possessions with determination
items.proc: Credit if the student tries to hold on to what is theirs when someone tries to grab it from them.

items.skill: Plays organised group games fairly (e.g. does not cheat in order to win)
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Can talk about difficult feelings (e.g. anger, sadness, worry) they experience
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Honours a simple bargain with the caregiver (e.g. can play outside only after cleaning/finishing their room)
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Watches responsibly over younger siblings/family members
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

items.skill: Cooperates with adults and peers in group situations to minimise quarrels and conflicts
items.proc: Parent report will suffice.

materials: Food: bread, biscuit, pieces of banana, individually wrapped sweet
4 pairs of different shapes with the same colour and size
4 pairs of the same shape but different size and colour
4 pieces each of graduated-size circles and squares
2 picture cards showing something silly or wrong
